title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns and Faces a Congressional Probe, Chris Van Hollen Challenges Chuck Schumer for Senate Leader, and Trump Pulls JD Vance Off Iran Talks
subhead: Nvidia names CFO Colette Kress interim CEO after Jensen Huang steps down and agrees to testify alongside Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick; Sen. Chris Van Hollen challenges Chuck Schumer after Democratic midterm gains; Trump halts Vance's Iran diplomacy and floats military action against Cuba; and Finland detects a strike on a Russian warship.

sections.heading: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Espionage Probe and Agrees to Testify Before Congress
sections.body:
According to BBC, The Guardian, and CNBC, Nvidia co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday after revelations of extramarital relationships involving two company subordinates and an intermediary—identified by Le Monde as Alice Huang—suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia appointed longtime chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO and veteran board member Harvey Jones as chair to steady the chipmaker, Financial Times reported.

Both Huang and US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have agreed to testify before congressional committees following a summons from Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott and House Foreign Affairs Chair Brian Mast, NBC News and The New York Times reported. Lawmakers from both parties are investigating whether the Commerce Department shielded Nvidia and failed to prevent the diversion of restricted AI accelerators to China.
sections.whyItMatters: Huang's sudden exit and the joint congressional summons of Nvidia's founder and the US Commerce Secretary turn a corporate governance scandal into a national-security investigation over US-China semiconductor export controls.

sections.heading: Chris Van Hollen Challenges Chuck Schumer for Senate Majority Leader After Midterm Sweep
sections.body:
According to The Guardian and AP News, Maryland Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen announced on Thursday that he will challenge veteran New York Senator Chuck Schumer for the post of US Senate Majority Leader in the incoming 120th Congress. Declaring that "the American people called for change" in last week's sweeping midterm victories, Van Hollen is backing calls from progressive and younger lawmakers for a more confrontational leadership posture during the final two years of the Trump presidency.

Meanwhile, in Washington, AP News reported that five people were shot near the capital—including one person killed at a gym—before the suspect took his own life, while incoming House members gathered on Capitol Hill for orientation ahead of a narrowly divided session.
sections.whyItMatters: Van Hollen's rare leadership challenge against Schumer signals deep generational and foreign-policy restlessness inside the enlarged Senate Democratic caucus.

sections.heading: Trump Orders Vance to Drop Iran Ceasefire Talks and Hints at Military Action Against Cuba
sections.body:
According to AP News and The Independent, US President Donald Trump ordered Vice President JD Vance to abandon backchannel ceasefire negotiations with Tehran and redirect his focus toward investigating alleged domestic corruption and fraud in Democratic-led states. Speaking separately to reporters, Trump claimed that Gulf Arab states had asked Washington to pause further strikes on Iran even as Iranian forces targeted a US radar installation in Bahrain, Al Jazeera reported.

Hours later, Trump called Cuba a "failed nation" and suggested he wants to topple the authorities in Havana before leaving office in 2028, refusing to rule out military force, Al Jazeera and Hürriyet reported. At the same time, Le Monde noted that Trump threatened Mexico with steeper import tariffs over migrant caravans moving toward the US border.
sections.whyItMatters: Sidelining Vance from Iran diplomacy while floating military intervention in Cuba and tariff hikes on Mexico shows the White House pivoting toward unilateral pressure after its midterm losses.

sections.heading: Finland Detects Strike on Russian Warship in Baltic Sea as Putin Agrees to European Talks Role
sections.body:
According to Al Jazeera and Defense News, Finland's military announced on Thursday that it detected a strike on a Russian warship in the Baltic Sea a day earlier, though Helsinki added that regional maritime security remains stable. The naval incident coincided with high-stakes diplomacy in Moscow and Dublin, where US envoy Jared Kushner and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed that Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to include European nations in the next round of Russia-Ukraine peace talks, France 24 and Financial Times reported.

In Kyiv, Zelenskyy also announced preparations for the largest prisoner-of-war exchange with Russia to date, Anadolu Agency reported, even as Ukrainian officials told NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte that SpaceX's Starshield military satellite communications were degraded again during the negotiations.
sections.whyItMatters: Bringing European capitals into the next negotiating round closes a major rift between Washington and Brussels, even as Baltic naval strikes and Starshield disruptions underscore active battlefield pressure.

sections.heading: Federal Reserve Drops Rate Vote From October 2027 Meeting as Yen Breaches 160
sections.body:
According to CNBC and The Wall Street Journal, the US Federal Reserve announced a policy calendar switch under which its October 26–27, 2027 Federal Open Market Committee meeting will be dedicated to long-term framework deliberation without a formal interest-rate vote or post-meeting statement, leaving seven rate-setting meetings next year. Meanwhile, US Treasury data showed the federal budget deficit jumped 42.1% year-over-year in October—the first month of fiscal 2027—to $404.1 billion, Bloomberg HT reported.

In Asia, Japan's finance minister vowed currency intervention after the yen weakened past the 160-per-dollar threshold, CNA reported, while Thailand prepared import duties of up to 30% on cross-border e-commerce parcels targeting low-cost Chinese vendors, according to the South China Morning Post. In the Caribbean, France 24 reported that Haitian police and Salvadoran troops recaptured Port-au-Prince's main national stadium after two years of gang control.
sections.whyItMatters: A $404.1 billion single-month US fiscal deficit and rising Treasury yields are driving the dollar above 160 yen and straining emerging-market trade balances.

bottomLine: Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia and congressional subpoenas for both Huang and Commerce Secretary Lutnick rattle the AI sector, while Sen. Chris Van Hollen's challenge to Chuck Schumer and Trump's halt to Vance's Iran talks reshape Washington's post-midterm power struggle.
sources: BBC, The Guardian, CNBC, Le Monde, Financial Times, NBC News, The New York Times, AP News, The Independent, Al Jazeera, Hürriyet, Defense News, France 24, Anadolu Agency, The Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg HT, CNA, South China Morning Post
